map: Taylor remainder bounds objective and gradient model errors.
A sufficiently large regularization coefficient guarantees a successful trial and bounds sigma_k.
Each nonterminal accepted step decreases f by at least epsilon^((p+1)/p)/kappa_s.
Coefficient growth controls the number of rejected trials.

assumptions: f:R^d->R is C^p, bounded below by f_low; ||D^p f(x)-D^p f(y)||_T <= (p-1)! L ||x-y||. Euclidean induced tensor norm.

statement.conclusion: Theorem 2.5 bounds successful steps by ceil(kappa_s (f(x0)-f_low)/epsilon^((p+1)/p)) and total trials by this bound times (1+|log gamma1|/log gamma2), plus log(sigma_max/sigma0)/log gamma2. For an implementation include initial/final checking evaluations explicitly; an additive O(1) does not affect the exponent.
statement.objects_and_definitions: T_p(x,s)=sum_{j=0}^p D^j f(x)[s]^j/j!; m(x,s,sigma)=T_p(x,s)+sigma||s||^(p+1)/(p+1). Parameters theta>0, 0<sigma_min<=sigma0, 0<eta1<=eta2<1, 0<gamma1<1<gamma2<gamma3. sigma_max=max{sigma0,gamma3 L(p+1)/[p(1-eta2)]}; kappa_s=(p+1)(L+theta+sigma_max)^((p+1)/p)/(eta1 sigma_min).
statement.parameter_domains: Integer p>=1; all algorithm constants fixed as specified.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For each epsilon>0 and admissible objective.
